#### “The situation is funny because everyone is so sold on other products, but those products are
#### awful compared to what I have in INFINITT PACS. For example, it takes me significantly less
#### time to make the same report in INFINITT PACS than it does in other systems. Also, for prior
#### sections, our current study comes up in INFINITT PACS, and the three priors populate the screen
#### just like they do in the other vendors’ products, but INFINITT PACS automatically populates our
#### prior fields. We looked at those priors because we brought them up on the screen, so there is
#### no reason that we should have to open our mouths to tell the voice recognition system that we
#### opened them and looked at them. There are also drop-down menus that I have built, and I can
#### click on a section in my field and select that, and I don’t even have to say a word. Reading in
#### INFINITT PACS is a breath of fresh air. There is a tremendous shortage of radiologists
#### nationwide, so anything that can make me more efficient is better, and INFINITT PACS does
#### that.”

VP/Executive

### “Overall, INFINITT has excellent products. If I were buying the same kind of products today,
### INFINITT’s product would definitely be my leading choice. I try to keep myself up to speed on
### INFINITT’s competition in case we ever decide to switch platforms, but so far, I haven’t seen
### any compelling reason to switch, even if making a switch would be easy. I am very happy with
### INFINITT. The vendor has taken a lot of our feedback and has really incorporated some changes
### that have made the product much more functional for us. The product was really good before, but
### INFINITT has done a better job of upgrading it now.”

Director

### “INFINITT’s support is very good. The vendor does exceedingly well in that area. I have had to
### make very few support calls, but when I do call, someone immediately picks up the phone and is
### on top of the issue. INFINITT’s support portal is very intuitive and easy to use. The support
### people have a large knowledge base, and they guide me in the right direction. We are a hands-on
### organization, so if we can do something without the support team, we will take a shot at it. But
### when we need assistance, someone at INFINITT immediately picks up the case.”

Manager

### “We use a different PACS at another facility, and the difference between that PACS and INFINITT
### PACS is night and day! We have so much flexibility with INFINITT PACS, and it’s the easiest
### product to integrate across facilities. Physicians who use the other PACS are now crying for
### this one!”

**George Jackson*

About Us

## The Imaging Expertise Your Research Deserves

At ANTS, we are dedicated to empowering our clients to advance the field of neuroimaging. As
research consultants, we deliver robust data processing solutions that enhance the utility of
advanced neuroimaging — enabling more accurate prognostication and improved therapeutic delivery.

Whether you need help designing a study, processing diffusion or functional MRI data, running the
right statistical analyses, or interpreting your results — our team of physician-scientists and
engineers works alongside you at every step.

[ANTS LLC logo — an ant head with neural circuit patterns]

What We Do

## Our Neuroimaging Services

End-to-end support for neuroimaging data — from collection to insight.

### Data Analysis & AI Solutions

ML/AI-powered analysis, statistical modeling, and advanced signal processing to extract meaningful
insights from complex neuroimaging data.
* Machine Learning
* AI
* Statistical Modeling
* Signal Processing

### Pipeline Development

Automated, reproducible data processing pipelines built for scale. Cloud-native workflows that take
you from raw acquisition to publication-ready results.
* Automation
* Cloud-Native
* Scalable Workflows

### Imaging Consultation

Expert guidance on study design, acquisition parameter optimization, and methodology review. We help
you ask better questions and build the infrastructure to answer them.
* Study Design
* Methodology
* Parameter Optimization

[Get Started][14]

Our Work

## Featured Projects

A selection of platforms and tools we've built for the neuroimaging community.

### Automated Analysis Platform

Developed a scalable cloud-based platform for automated processing and analysis of large-scale
neuroimaging datasets.
* Cloud Platform
* Automation
* AI

### Clinical Decision Support Tool

Built an ML-powered tool to assist clinicians in interpreting complex imaging data for improved
patient outcomes.
* Machine Learning
* Clinical
* Decision Support

### Multi-Site Data Pipeline

Engineered a robust data processing pipeline supporting multi-site research studies with harmonized
imaging protocols.
* Pipeline
* Multi-Site
* Data Harmonization

### Research Analytics Dashboard

Created an interactive visualization platform for exploring and analyzing processed neuroimaging
results across studies.
* Visualization
* Analytics
* Dashboard

About Us

## The Imaging Expertise Your Research Deserves

At ANTS, we are dedicated to empowering our clients to advance the field of neuroimaging. As
research consultants, we deliver robust data processing solutions that enhance the utility of
advanced neuroimaging — enabling more accurate prognostication and improved therapeutic delivery.

Whether you need help designing a study, processing diffusion or functional MRI data, running the
right statistical analyses, or interpreting your results — our team of physician-scientists and
engineers works alongside you at every step.

[ANTS LLC logo — an ant head with neural circuit patterns]

What We Do

## Our Neuroimaging Services

End-to-end support for neuroimaging data — from collection to insight.

### Data Analysis & AI Solutions

ML/AI-powered analysis, statistical modeling, and advanced signal processing to extract meaningful
insights from complex neuroimaging data.
* Machine Learning
* AI
* Statistical Modeling
* Signal Processing

### Pipeline Development

Automated, reproducible data processing pipelines built for scale. Cloud-native workflows that take
you from raw acquisition to publication-ready results.
* Automation
* Cloud-Native
* Scalable Workflows

### Imaging Consultation

Expert guidance on study design, acquisition parameter optimization, and methodology review. We help
you ask better questions and build the infrastructure to answer them.
* Study Design
* Methodology
* Parameter Optimization

opinions, all designed to improve the quality of pharmacotherapy and healthcare outcomes.

## Ivan Đikić: Science, Innovation, and the Fight Against Disease

Professor Ivan Đikić, a world-renowned scientist from Goethe University Frankfurt, shares insights
into his groundbreaking research on the molecular foundations of human diseases. His pioneering work
focuses on the ubiquitin system — a critical regulator of protein quality control and immune
function. Defects in this system are linked to major health challenges, including cancer,
Parkinson’s disease, Alzheimer’s disease, and immune disorders. Professor Đikić is also a leading
voice in the development of precision medicine, advocating for the integration of genomics and
molecular signaling to create more effective, personalized therapies. He emphasizes the need to make
advanced treatments accessible to all and inspires young scientists to embrace interdisciplinary
collaboration and innovation in research.

### CURRY for Epilepsy Evaluation

CURRY is an ideal platform for combining and processing the various datasets that are obtained from
a patient during an epilepsy evaluation. CURRY combines multiple data sets (EEG, ECoG, MEG, MRI,
fMRI, CT, DTI, and PET) to ensure the maximum information from the patients complete data set is
utilized in making critical decisions. An overview of [CURRY for epilepsy evaluation][46] and
[video][47] provide a brief overview of the clinically related features of the CURRY Neuroimaging
Suite.

[Electrode localization]

### Electrode localization

You have only one opportunity -- make the most of it! You took the time to position the electrodes
accurately, so it should be worth the time to measure their locations with respect to surface
landmarks to enhance future signal analysis options.  3D locations of electrodes can be used in
co-registration of surface measured physiological signals with anatomical MRI, CT and other imaging
modalities in software applications such as EMSE Suite and others.  Quick and accurate measurement
of 3D electrode positions adds only 3-5 minutes to a typical study, but it ensures precision when
coregistering surface measurements with anatomical images.

real-time insights into brain activity. Our portable, non-invasive systems allow researchers to
study cognitive functions, brain connectivity, and hemodynamic responses in a wide range of
environments—from labs to real-world settings.

space.

VR-environment scenarios for specialized research needs.

# Research

Sleep fulfills vital functions for the brain and body. However, sleep is not a uniform state:
alternating substates and oscillation patterns show rich variations on different time scales. In the
Sleep & Memory Lab, based at the [Donders Institute][8] in Nijmegen, The Netherlands, we aim to
uncover the mechanisms behind this variability and their specific role in the functions of sleep. We
are particularly interested in the following topics:

─────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[[sle│[**Sleep physiology.**][10] From an evolutionary point of view, spending hours in a           
ep]][│non-responsive state seems strikingly non-adaptive. Sleep thus serves several vital functions 
9]   │to overcompensate for this disadvantage. In our lab, we develop new strategies to understand  
     │the structure of sleep on the micro- (sleep stages and microprocesses), meso- (sleep cycles), 
     │and macro-level (sleep regularity), with the aim to map the richness of sleep physiology to   
     │the different functions of sleep.                                                             
─────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[[cli│[**Clinical applications.**][12] Sleep disturbances are the leading transdiagnostic symptom of
nical│and likely causal contributor to the development of psychiatric and neurological diseases. We 
]][11│focus in particular on two areas of mental health to help translate sleep research insights   
]    │into clinical applications and health care innovations: How is sleep involved stress-related  
     │disorders, and how is brain clearance during sleep impaired in neurodegenerative diseases?    
─────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[[met│[**Sleep research methods.**][14] Polysomnography as the gold standard in sleep research      
hods]│generates rich and multimodal datasets. However, considering the massive costs and thus       
][13]│resulting small sample sizes of this method, we help to transfer sleep research from          
     │small-scale lab environments to large-scale clinical and home settings. We develop and        
     │validate new tools for the recording and analysis of sleep data, from minimal sleep EEG       
     │headbands to analysis pipelines for big sleep data.                                           
─────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[[luc│[**Dreaming.**][16] Conscious experience fluctuates considerably across the sleep-wake cycle: 
id   │alert attention alternates with mind wandering, sleep onset imagery, dreamless sleep and vivid
dream│dreaming. We study consciousness during sleep, considering the phenomenon of lucid dreaming   
ing]]│particularly interesting as both a model case and tool. In addition to fundamental insights   
[15] │into the functions and neural correlates of dreaming, we develop and validate different dream 
     │engineering strategies to modulate dream experiences.                                         
─────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[[mne│[**Memory.**][18] Memory skills differ across the general population – from age-related memory
monic│decline to the outstanding feats of memory champions. In addition to the role of sleep in     
s]][1│memory processing, we investigate different strategies of learning and memory enhancement,    
7]   │with a focus on the mnemonic training strategies used in memory sports. Beyond the efficacy of
     │mnemonics in naïve subjects, developmental contexts and age-related decline, we are           
     │particularly interested in the neural mechanisms underlying mnemonic training and superior    
     │memory skills.                                                                                
─────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

[Participate in our studies!][19]

# Precision In Neuroscience

## Advancing medicine through the provision of precision imaging biomarker insights for the
## discovery, development and delivery of novel treatments in neurological disease

[ IXI™ Platform ][59]
[ Services ][60]

## A global leader in neuroimaging and biomarker analytics

[ Company ][61]

IXI™ is IXICO’s proprietary, AI-enabled neuroimaging technology platform for precision medicine,
purpose-built to drive clinical trial imaging and biomarker science insights in neurological disease
research.

The Platform, combined with IXICO's expert clinical trial operations, helps accelerate
decision-making in clinical research and maximise the potential of drug development programmes.

## Neuroscience Expertise

IXICO has built a global reputation as a leading end-to-end Imaging Contract Research Organisation
(iCRO), expertly managing and analysing neurological clinical trials.

The Company is a key part of the global neurological disease research community, with a 20-year
proven track record in the biopharmaceutical industry, working with leading pharma companies,
innovative biotechs, scientific consortia, and non-profit organisations.

[ Therapeutic Expertise ][62]

## Differentiated Technology

[ IXI™ Platform ][63]

The IXI™ Platform is tailor-made for neurological diseases, reliably managing global clinical trial
data, precisely reading radiological scans, and measuring key imaging biomarkers linked to the
identification, progression, and treatment of conditions such as Alzheimer’s, Huntington’s, and
Parkinson’s disease.

# Defining the future of brain health

The only technology for accessible and evidence-based measurements of the brain.

[Experience it yourself][7]

## The core principles behind our products

### Actionable

Leveraging advanced algorithms to drive improvements in brain health and develop new interventions.

[Offer Kernel Scans at your clinic →][8]

### Science-backed

We lead with robust science and engage with leaders in the community.

[Read our publications →][9]

### Differentiated

A deep technology platform that both scales and breaks through the limitations of those that came
before.

[Learn more about the technology →][10]

## From brain data to insight

Kernel delivers detailed information about brain function by combining our non-invasive brain
measurements with algorithmic advances. You can now reliably track the performance of your brain.
1. Book a scan with one of our partner clinics
2. Get scanned in 30 minutes or less
3. Review your results with our user-friendly reports
4. Consult with your health team and see how interventions change your brain health

[Find a location][11][See what to expect][12]
[Platform]

## Follow your brain function over time

Unlike genetics, our brains are constantly changing and regular measurement is important to
understand what factors create the biggest changes in function.

Kernel's longitudinal reports let you visualize your cognitive health so you and your clinician can
track these changes, measure progress, and optimize interventions.

## Built for wellness and medicine

Discover our industry-leading tracer wellness products and learn more about our
upcoming marer medical products.

[Wellness]
[Wellness]

### Brain Agetracer

We track our step count and sleep quality, now you can track your brain health. Brain Age is an
objective measure of health built from thousands of scans.

[Book a scan with one of our clinics →][13]

### Cognitiontracer

The only cognitive tracker designed to assess healthy brains. Receive a detailed composition report
of key cognitive domains and see how your cognitive performance stacks up to others.

[Book a scan with one of our clinics →][14]

### Depressionmarer

Our depression study investigates whether brain activity can help predict if patients will respond
to TMS and Spravato® (esketamine) treatments. Early results suggest Kernel Flow may offer new
insights for selecting the right treatment for the right patient at the right time.

[Learn more about our ongoing work →][15]

### Cognitionmarer

In a published study, Kernel Flow successfully detected early patterns of brain activity associated
with mild cognitive impairment (MCI). This result highlights the platform's potential to support
early identification of cognitive decline in clinical settings. Additional studies are being planned
to assess more detailed profiles of cognitive performance in the context of disease diagnostics.

[Read our recent publication →][16]

Want to participate in a paid research study that helps our team develop the next generation of
brain health tools?

#### [ From Compliance to Clinical Action: Fixing the Broken Loop in Post-Market Surveillance ][24]

By Aalap Patel, MS, CQE, CSSBB

Post-market surveillance (PMS) systems in the medical device industry have become increasingly
sophisticated in collecting complaints, monitoring adverse events, and generating regulatory
reports. However, many organizations still struggle to translate these insights into timely clinical
action and meaningful patient safety improvements. This article examines the growing disconnect
between regulatory reporting and operational decision-making, explores the challenges of signal
detection and prioritization, and outlines practical strategies for building closed-loop PMS systems
that improve patient safety outcomes and organizational responsiveness.

## About MEG technology

### **What is MEG?**

MEG identifies the very small magnetic fields when brain cells are active, to detect and record
normal and abnormal brain activity in “real time.” MEG can localize brain function to within a
centimeter or even millimeters of the activity. MEG adds to the hemodynamic data obtained from MR
technology.

### **Comfortable patient experience**

It is entirely non-invasive, silent, and with no applied magnetic fields, radiation or injections of
any kind.

### **Precise technology for clinical treatment planning**

MEG helps doctors locate normal brain activity inluding where the brain processes language, sensory,
and motor information to help plan surgical and non-surgical treatments. MEG is unaffected by the
skull and scalp, or hemodynamic data like MR.

## MEG is an important part of pre-surgical evaluation

MEG Maps™ is designed to push the boundaries of neuroscience by augmenting the performance
limitations of traditional MR imaging modalities, providing neuroscientists, neurologists and
oncologists with a more advanced and precise functional imaging tool.

MEG is used alongside other functional brain mapping methods, such as fMRI, PET, SPECT, and TMS, to
non-invasively provide clinicians with a more complete picture of the location of a patient’s normal
and abnormal brain activity. MEG can assist in the presurgical evaluation and treatment planning,
specifically the placement of intracranial EEG (iEEG).

## MEG is an important part of a research program

Thousands of patients are participating in clinical MEG studies focusing on epilepsy, brain tumors,
traumatic brain injuries, PTSD, stroke, dementias, Parkinson’s, and other neurodegenerative
disorders.

MEG can be a valuable tool in Phase I & III pharmaceutical drug development as it allows researchers
to gain insights into the neural mechanisms underlying the effects of a drug.

## About MEG technology

### **What is MEG?**

MEG identifies the very small magnetic fields when brain cells are active, to detect and record
normal and abnormal brain activity in “real time.” MEG can localize brain function to within a
centimeter or even millimeters of the activity. MEG adds to the hemodynamic data obtained from MR
technology.

### **Comfortable patient experience**

It is entirely non-invasive, silent, and with no applied magnetic fields, radiation or injections of
any kind.

### **Precise technology for clinical treatment planning**

MEG helps doctors locate normal brain activity inluding where the brain processes language, sensory,
and motor information to help plan surgical and non-surgical treatments. MEG is unaffected by the
skull and scalp, or hemodynamic data like MR.

## MEG is an important part of pre-surgical evaluation

MEG Maps™ is designed to push the boundaries of neuroscience by augmenting the performance
limitations of traditional MR imaging modalities, providing neuroscientists, neurologists and
oncologists with a more advanced and precise functional imaging tool.

MEG is used alongside other functional brain mapping methods, such as fMRI, PET, SPECT, and TMS, to
non-invasively provide clinicians with a more complete picture of the location of a patient’s normal
and abnormal brain activity. MEG can assist in the presurgical evaluation and treatment planning,
specifically the placement of intracranial EEG (iEEG).

## MEG is an important part of a research program

Thousands of patients are participating in clinical MEG studies focusing on epilepsy, brain tumors,
traumatic brain injuries, PTSD, stroke, dementias, Parkinson’s, and other neurodegenerative
disorders.

MEG can be a valuable tool in Phase I & III pharmaceutical drug development as it allows researchers
to gain insights into the neural mechanisms underlying the effects of a drug.

### Why Neuroimaging

Neuroimaging can play a role in drug development at all stages of the process, pre-clinical to phase
IV.  In pre-clinical it can be used for validating animal models.  In phase I, it can be used to
better establish dose response curves, aid in the shifting the proof of concept (POC) from late to
early phase, and identifying additional/alternative targets for late stage study.  In phases II &
III, it can aid and/or serve, thanks to the recent passage of passage of the 21st Century Cures
Act[^{I}][1], as proof of efficacy.  In phase IV, it can be used to provide differentiation between
available treatments.

Focusing here just on POC, the CNS drug pipeline has stymied, with CNS drugs 45% less likely to
proceed to regulatory filling than non-CNS drugs[^{II}][2]. Failures in CNS drugs are due in large
part to failures to demonstrate efficacy in Phase III, with rates significantly higher than non-CNS
drugs[^{II}][3]. While phase III attrition rates are significantly higher for CNS drugs, it is not
the case for phase II. Putting it in other words CNS drugs fail late in trials predominately for
efficacy when compared to other drugs. These late stage failures are costly both in time and in
dollars.

#### Dwindling Numbers Along the CNS Drug Pipeline[^{iii}][4]^{,}[^{v}][5]

Figure 1: Dwindling Numbers in the traditional CNS Drug Discovery Pipeline. For CNS drugs the
average discontinuation rate for the clinical trial phase is 99.6%.

#### Reasons for Phase III Discontinuations[^{II}][6]

Figure 2: Proportion of Phase III discontinuations by primary cause.

To quote the former director of National Institutes of Mental Health (NIMH), Dr. Thomas
Insel[^{III}][7], “Given that over 95% of compounds fail during the clinical phases of development
(a fact not appreciated by looking at the published literature which is biased towards positive
results), success may require rapid failures in order to conserve resources by moving quickly to the
next candidate (“fast-fail”[^{IV}][8])."  The “fast-fail, quick win” model (see figure below) is one
where the proof of concept (POC) is shifted earlier in the clinical trials, from phases II & III to
phase I, from on or after the first effective dose (FED) to the first human dose (FHD) or shortly
thereafter.

Shifting the POC earlier, will increase attrition in earlier stages, but will also increase the
probability of success in the new molecular entities (NME’s) that make it through phase I.  This
“fast-fail” approach allows a culling of the pipeline early on, reducing cost[^{V}][9].  The savings
estimate due to this shift is on the order of $30 Million dollars in out-of-pocket expenses per
NME[^{IV}][10].  This savings can be used to fund approximately 2 additional NME phase I
studies[^{IV}][11].

#### Quick Win - Fast Fail Model^{[III][12]}

Figure 3: Paul, S., et al.'s Quick Win / Fast-Fail Model - The idea behind it is to shift the Proof
of Concept (POC) in human for new molecular entities from phases II & III in clinical trials to
phase I. By shifting the POC earlier the attrition in can be shifted earlier leading to a higher
probability of success in later stages, in turn leading to tremendous savings in time and money. In
addition, to shifting attrition, NMEs can readily returned to preclinical stages if alternative
targets are found during phase I.

This POC shift to early phase requires the support of surrogate measures. Positron Emission
Tomography (PET) has long been considered the main avenue for surrogate makers in CNS clinical
trials, whether through biodistribution, receptor occupancy/binding or measuring metabolic changes
in the target using FDG or FDOPA[^{VI}][13].  Unfortunately, biodistribution and receptor
occupancy/binding are only a part of a POC, that is, they show that the drug in question is finding
the target, but show nothing on whether or not it is modulating the target circuit in a meaningful
way.  FDG & FDOPA have the potential to measure target modulation, but they are slow (low temporal
resolution) and blunt (low spatial resolution) tools, and as such they miss many meaningful
signals.  Where PET fails in measuring functional change other neuroimaging modalities can be
brought to bear.  These include but are not limited to: fMRI, ASL, qEEG, EEG-fMRI, EEG source
imaging, NIRS, & MEG.

#### What is Functional Neuroimaging & What can it do

FMRI and other imaging modalities such as qEEG, EEG-fMRI, EEG source, MEG and NIRS are quantitative
based tools, providing researchers and business leaders with statistical decision making power.

Since its inception roughly 25 years ago functional magnetic resonance imagining (fMRI)
[^{VII}][14]^{, } [^{VIII}][15]^{, &} [^{IX}][16] has opened up a new realm of possibilities with
neuroimaging. It has confirmed[^{X}][17], debunked[^{XI}][18] as well as opened new
understandings[^{XII}][19] of how the mind works. When taking the whole family of non-invasive
neuroimaging modalities into account it has by far the highest spatial resolution with some studies
using resolutions on the order of sub millimeter[^{X}][20]. With all of its accolades and the
beautiful pictures it creates, fMRI still has highly limited temporal resolution with the current
upper limit of its sampling rate being on the order of hundreds of milliseconds[^{XIII}][21].

Electroencephalography (EEG) fMRI’s much older cousin has been around for over a century[^{XIV}][22]
and gave some of the first views into the active mind. Even now it is still the key measurement for
sleep staging[^{XV}][23]^{, }[^{XVI}][24] and for diagnosing many neurological disorders such as
epilepsy[^{XVII}][25] and schizophrenia[^{XVIII}][26]. EEG, whose instrumentation is technologically
primitive when compared with that of fMRI, leaves it in the proverbial dust in that EEG has
essentially limitless temporal resolution. EEG spatial resolution on the other hand is more of an
inference than a certainty in that in its native domain it a measurement of electrical potential
differences on the scalp. Transforming these measures across the scalp into the space of the brain
is done through a process referred to as source localization. Source localization’s resolution is on
the order of one to two centimeters[^{XIX}][27].

## Welcome **Message**



 

**Dear Esteemed Participants and Distinguished Colleagues,**

It is with great pleasure that we welcome you to the 8th Global Conclave on Neurology and
Neurological Disorders" (NEURO Conclave 2027) taking place on June 21–22, 2027 in Singapore. This
conference brings together world-renowned experts and thought leaders in neurology, I really found
the conference both enriching and insightful., providing an excellent platform for collaboration and
knowledge exchange.[Read more][56]...
 

 


 

**Dear Valued Colleagues and Friends,**

 

Translating purpose and mindset into positive impact through shared vision, compassion, and
collaborative spirit established at Neuro Conclave 2026 in Singapore—where neurologists, clinicians,
researchers, educators, advocates, public health leaders, and policymakers from around the world
came together to advance evidence-based care, promote equity, foster innovation, and combat
stigma—we are delighted to invite you to the 8th Global Conclave on Neurology and Neurological
Disorders (Neuro Conclave 2027), to be held on June 21–22, 2027 in Singapore. [Read more][57]...

 


 

**Dear Esteemed Participants and Distinguished Colleagues,**

Welcome to NEURO Conclave 2027!

It was a pleasure to participate in NEURO Conclave 2026 and to meet colleagues from many different
countries, all working to improve our understanding of neurological and neurodevelopmental
conditions. What I appreciated most was the opportunity to exchange knowledge, discuss new ideas,

Featured tool/resource

[Graphic for MRIcroGL]

# MRIcroGL

MRIcroGL allows you to view 2D slices and renderings of your brain imaging data. It can display many
image formats and includes a graphical interface for dcm2nii to convert DICOM images to NIfTI
format. It allows you to draw regions of interest which can aid lesion mapping and fMRI analysis. It
provides sophisticated rendering.

Featured tool/resource

[Graphic for eeg_pipelines]

# eeg_pipelines

This repository contains 4 stand-alone pipelines (along with one test dataset), in EEGLAB,
Fieldtrip, Brainstorm, and MNE. There is also a link to the HAPPE EEGLAB-based pipeline. The
pipelines have been optimized to process event-related potential and are described in the associated
manuscript. All pipelines run on the sample data provided although they do require a separate
installation of the corresponding software packages.

Based on our scanning of the hyperparameter space for artifact rejection and preprocessing, these
are the best automated EEG pipelines for EEGLAB, Fieldtrip, Brainstorm, and MNE to process ERP. Test
them yourself by plugging in your data.

Featured tool/resource

[Graphic for BabelBrain: Planning software for Transcranial Ultrasound Stimulation]

# BabelBrain: Planning software for Transcranial Ultrasound Stimulation

BabelBrain is an open-source standalone graphic-user-interface application designed for studies of
neuromodulation using transcranial ultrasound stimulation (TUS). It calculates the transmitted
acoustic field in the brain tissue, taking into account the distortion effects caused by the skull
barrier. The simulation is prepared using scans from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and, if
available, computed tomography (CT) and zero-echo time MRI scans. It also calculates the thermal
effects based on a given ultrasound regime, such as the total duration of exposure, the duty cycle,
and acoustic intensity. The tool is designed to work in tandem with neuronavigation and
visualization software, such as 3DSlicer. BabelBrain supports multiple GPU backends, including
Metal, OpenCL, and CUDA, and works on all major operating systems, including Linux, macOS, and
Windows. This tool is particularly optimized for Apple ARM64 systems, which are common in brain
imaging research.

Featured tool/resource

[Graphic for BrainEffeX]

# BrainEffeX

Effect size estimation is crucial for power analysis and experiment deisgn, but poses unique
challenges in fMRI research due to the complexity of the data and analysis techniques. Here, we
utalized large fMRI datasets to obtain precise univariate and multivariate effect size estimates
from "typical" fMRI study designs: brain-behavior correlation, task vs. rest, and between-group
analyses of functional connecitivity and task-based activation maps. This is an interactive web
application for exploring these effect maps.

can dramatically improve. And when pharmaceutical companies have a higher probability of success in

world, is wholly dedicated to aspiring to build tools and software that analyze brain images and
other markers of neurodegeneration to create the clearest, most accurate and reliable predictors and
objective measures of CNS disorders.

# ABOUT RHOVICA

SoNav Platform : transforming blind neurosurgery into guided precision

#### Today : no visibility

Clinicians treating brain emergencies, such as severe trauma or brain bleeding, need to act quickly
and precisely. Without direct imaging, they rely on pre-acquired CT scans to guide procedures,
images that become unreliable intraoperatively, as brain shift may alter the anatomy any time.

#### Our technology

Rhovica’s instrument-embedded technology is able to continuously capture live data from inside the
brain, delivering real-time imaging of the brain without any external imaging equipment.

####  Patented IP

Rhovica’s core technology is protected by several patent families. The intellectual property is
fully owned by Rhovica Neuoimaging AG, providing a strong foundation for defensible market
positioning.

#### SoNav® I

External Ventricular Drain (EVD) placement is on of the most basic and often performed neurosurgical
procedures and can be life-saving. Freehand bedside EVD placement relies solely anatomical landmarks
with up to 28% misplacement rate, multiple passes and risk of hemorrhage.  

SoNav™  is an innovative EVD catheter equipped with integrated miniaturized sensors providing
real-time visualization of brain ventricule directly at the patient’s bedside. 

Our novel EVD catheter SoNav™ allows a fast and secure placement of external ventricular drains as
well as real-time monitoring after insertion for elevated ICP emergencies. 

# TEAM

Executive Team Advisory Team Board of Directors

#### Dr. med. Martin Hlavica

##### Neurosurgeon, Co-Founder & Chief Executive Officer (CEO)

Board-certified neurosurgeon with 500+ neurosurgical interventions, completing residency in
University Hospitals Zurich and Inselspital Bern, driven by evidence-based medicine, (co-)author of
>20 publications in peer-reviewed journals and speaker at international congresses. Ambitious to
make an impact in patient’s treatment with high interest in business creation and economics.
* [ ][15]

#### Blair Fraser, BSc

##### Chief Business Officer (CBO)

Blair has over 35 years of global medical device experience and serves as Chief Business Officer. He
is skilled in a wide range of corporate functions, including general management, global
evidence-based marketing, strategic analysis and planning, mergers, acquisitions and strategic
alliances, and scientific and medical affairs. He has experience of start-up, rapid growth, and
established MedTech companies, with a proven track record of new market identification, penetration
with new technologies, KOL network building, and sustainably increasing market share.
* [ ][16]

#### Dr. med. univ. Thomas Rhomberg

##### Neurosurgeon, Co-Founder & Chief Medical Officer (CMO)

Thomas Rhomberg is the company`s co-founder and board-certified Neurosurgeon currently working as an
attending Neurosurgeon in Austria. He completed his MD from the Medical University of Innsbruck with
a research exchange at the Harvard Medical School. Previous parts of his neurosurgical were
completed at the University Hospital of Bern (Inselspital) and the Kantonsspital St. Gallen. He is
driven by the desire to translate the latest technology into improved patient care.
* [ ][17]

#### Saeid Kasiri, PhD

##### Chief Technology Officer (CTO)

Engineer by training, Saeid has over 15 years of R&D experience in leading and developing Class
II/III medical devices, including active, implantable, and catheter-based technologies. He has
dedicated most of his career to startups and SMEs, with a successful track record of leading
cross-functional teams, design control, and risk management. Saeid translates unmet clinical needs
into innovative and effective design solutions.
* [ ][18]

#### Martin Fuchs

##### Vice President Quality, Governance & Compliance

Martin Fuchs has many years of sales experience in the healthcare sector and is experienced in
conception and realization of eHealth software solutions and Quality Systems.

### Sabi Cap.

A beanie. Securely and wirelessly, understands your thoughts and what you attempt to speak.

AI agents do whatever you can think of. Literally.

## The ScienceBehind PreciseBrain Reading
* Step 01
  
  Brain imaging with novel neuroimaging sensors powered by custom ASICs
* Step 02
  
  We collect a lot of brain imaging data (the world's largest neural decoding dataset)
* Step 03
  
  Map brain signals → thoughts using the world's most capable Brain Foundation Model

Aqvesme’s FDA Milestone: Expanding Mitapivat’s Reach in Thalassemia Treatment
][9]
22 January 2026
The FDA’s recent approval of Aqvesme (mitapivat) for the treatment of anemia in adults with alpha-
and beta-thalassemia marks a significant expansion for pyruvate kinase (PK) activators. By enhancing
the activity of the wild-type PK enzyme, Aqvesme improves red blood cell health and hemoglobin
levels, offering a potent oral alternative to chronic transfusions for patients regardless of their
specific genetic mutation. This broad indication underscores a major shift in metabolic regulation
therapy, requiring R&D teams to leverage deep structural intelligence to map the competitive
landscape of PK activators and identify future modification opportunities for next-generation
erythroid therapies.

The $4B Patent Cliff: Navigating the Generic Surge as Astellas’ Xtandi Nears Expiration
][13]
22 January 2026
Astellas Pharma is facing a defining moment as its blockbuster prostate cancer therapy, Xtandi
(enzalutamide), approaches a massive patent cliff in 2026 and 2027. With billions in annual revenue
at risk, the pharmaceutical giant is pivoting toward aggressive lifecycle management and strategic
BD (Business Development) to offset the impending generic competition. For generic manufacturers and
oncology innovators, this transition creates a high-stakes environment where the ability to rapidly
deconstruct original patent claims and identify "late-stage" IP vulnerabilities is the key to
capturing market share in a post-Xtandi era.

### [2026 BIO International Convention In-Depth Analysis Report][17]

The 2026 BIO International Convention, held June 22-25, 2026 at the San Diego Convention Center,
marked a pivotal moment for the biotechnology industry. With nearly 20,000 attendees from over 76
countries (43% international), the event showcased a resurgent biotech sector characterized by
record-breaking deal activity, accelerated AI adoption, and renewed investor confidence. The
convention's theme, "Driven by Purpose," underscored the industry's commitment to transforming
scientific breakthroughs into life-changing therapies. Notable highlights included a landmark $2.5
billion AI-powered drug discovery collaboration, over $100 billion in M&A activity, approximately
70,000 partnering meetings, and transformative regulatory updates from the FDA and EMA.

[[EHA 2026 | ATG vs PTCY GVHD Prophylaxis Clinical Outcome Analysis Report]][19]

### [EHA 2026 | ATG vs PTCY GVHD Prophylaxis Clinical Outcome Analysis Report][20]

Abstract: EHA-7202 Short: LB5009 The question of whether post-transplant cyclophosphamide (PTCy)
should replace anti-thymocyte globulin (ATG/ATLG) as the standard GVHD prophylaxis backbone in
HLA-compatible 10/10 matched unrelated donor (MUD) hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) has now
been directly addressed by a large, prospective randomized controlled trial presented at EHA 2026 by
Prof. Johannes Schetelig (Dresden, Germany) and co-investigators including Matthias Stelljes. The
trial — designated the GRAPPA study — concludes that ATG-based prophylaxis retains its
standard-of-care position in this specific setting, with PTCy failing to demonstrate superiority on
the primary composite endpoint. This finding is contextualized against a backdrop of registry data,
meta-analyses, and prior Phase 2/3 evidence that had generated significant debate about PTCy's
potential to displace ATG in the 10/10 MUD context.

The FDA’s recent approval of Aqvesme (mitapivat) for the treatment of anemia in adults with alpha-
and beta-thalassemia marks a significant expansion for pyruvate kinase (PK) activators. By enhancing
the activity of the wild-type PK enzyme, Aqvesme improves red blood cell health and hemoglobin
levels, offering a potent oral alternative to chronic transfusions for patients regardless of their
specific genetic mutation. This broad indication underscores a major shift in metabolic regulation
therapy, requiring R&D teams to leverage deep structural intelligence to map the competitive
landscape of PK activators and identify future modification opportunities for next-generation

[[EHA 2026 | ATG vs PTCY GVHD Prophylaxis Clinical Outcome Analysis Report]][19]

### [EHA 2026 | ATG vs PTCY GVHD Prophylaxis Clinical Outcome Analysis Report][20]

Abstract: EHA-7202 Short: LB5009 The question of whether post-transplant cyclophosphamide (PTCy)
should replace anti-thymocyte globulin (ATG/ATLG) as the standard GVHD prophylaxis backbone in
HLA-compatible 10/10 matched unrelated donor (MUD) hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) has now
been directly addressed by a large, prospective randomized controlled trial presented at EHA 2026 by
Prof. Johannes Schetelig (Dresden, Germany) and co-investigators including Matthias Stelljes. The
trial — designated the GRAPPA study — concludes that ATG-based prophylaxis retains its
standard-of-care position in this specific setting, with PTCy failing to demonstrate superiority on
the primary composite endpoint. This finding is contextualized against a backdrop of registry data,
meta-analyses, and prior Phase 2/3 evidence that had generated significant debate about PTCy's
potential to displace ATG in the 10/10 MUD context.

[[EHA 2026 | BRUIN CLL-322: Clinical Outcome Analysis Report]][22]

### [EHA 2026 | BRUIN CLL-322: Clinical Outcome Analysis Report][23]

Abstract: EHA-7224 Short: LB5001 BRUIN CLL-322 (NCT04965493) is the first randomized Phase 3 trial
to evaluate a non-covalent BTK inhibitor–based triplet regimen in previously treated CLL/SLL. With a
data cutoff of February 2, 2026, and results presented at EHA 2026, the trial demonstrated that
fixed-duration pirtobrutinib + venetoclax–rituximab (PVR) significantly improved progression-free
survival over venetoclax–rituximab (VenR) alone, meeting its primary endpoint across all key
subgroups. Overall survival data were not yet mature but trended in favor of PVR. This represents
Lilly's fourth Phase 3 CLL win for pirtobrutinib (Jaypirca®) and positions PVR as a potential new
standard of care in the relapsed/refractory setting.

enhance reading workflow, to support diagnostic accuracy and to enrich the user experience.

About Us

## The Imaging Expertise Your Research Deserves

At ANTS, we are dedicated to empowering our clients to advance the field of neuroimaging. As
research consultants, we deliver robust data processing solutions that enhance the utility of
advanced neuroimaging — enabling more accurate prognostication and improved therapeutic delivery.

Whether you need help designing a study, processing diffusion or functional MRI data, running the
right statistical analyses, or interpreting your results — our team of physician-scientists and
engineers works alongside you at every step.

[ANTS LLC logo — an ant head with neural circuit patterns]

What We Do

## Our Neuroimaging Services

End-to-end support for neuroimaging data — from collection to insight.

### Data Analysis & AI Solutions

ML/AI-powered analysis, statistical modeling, and advanced signal processing to extract meaningful
insights from complex neuroimaging data.
* Machine Learning
* AI
* Statistical Modeling
* Signal Processing

### Pipeline Development

Automated, reproducible data processing pipelines built for scale. Cloud-native workflows that take
you from raw acquisition to publication-ready results.
* Automation
* Cloud-Native
* Scalable Workflows

### Imaging Consultation

Expert guidance on study design, acquisition parameter optimization, and methodology review. We help
you ask better questions and build the infrastructure to answer them.
* Study Design
* Methodology
* Parameter Optimization

[Get Started][14]

Our Work

## Featured Projects

A selection of platforms and tools we've built for the neuroimaging community.

### Automated Analysis Platform

Developed a scalable cloud-based platform for automated processing and analysis of large-scale
neuroimaging datasets.
* Cloud Platform
* Automation
* AI

### Clinical Decision Support Tool

Built an ML-powered tool to assist clinicians in interpreting complex imaging data for improved
patient outcomes.
* Machine Learning
* Clinical
* Decision Support

### Multi-Site Data Pipeline

Engineered a robust data processing pipeline supporting multi-site research studies with harmonized
imaging protocols.
* Pipeline
* Multi-Site
* Data Harmonization

### Research Analytics Dashboard

Created an interactive visualization platform for exploring and analyzing processed neuroimaging
results across studies.
* Visualization
* Analytics
* Dashboard

## Ivan Đikić: Science, Innovation, and the Fight Against Disease

Professor Ivan Đikić, a world-renowned scientist from Goethe University Frankfurt, shares insights
into his groundbreaking research on the molecular foundations of human diseases. His pioneering work
focuses on the ubiquitin system — a critical regulator of protein quality control and immune
function. Defects in this system are linked to major health challenges, including cancer,
Parkinson’s disease, Alzheimer’s disease, and immune disorders. Professor Đikić is also a leading
voice in the development of precision medicine, advocating for the integration of genomics and
molecular signaling to create more effective, personalized therapies. He emphasizes the need to make
advanced treatments accessible to all and inspires young scientists to embrace interdisciplinary
collaboration and innovation in research.

### CURRY for Epilepsy Evaluation

CURRY is an ideal platform for combining and processing the various datasets that are obtained from
a patient during an epilepsy evaluation. CURRY combines multiple data sets (EEG, ECoG, MEG, MRI,
fMRI, CT, DTI, and PET) to ensure the maximum information from the patients complete data set is
utilized in making critical decisions. An overview of [CURRY for epilepsy evaluation][46] and
[video][47] provide a brief overview of the clinically related features of the CURRY Neuroimaging
Suite.

# Large format scanners and imaging matter to us

scanners. We continuously strive to improve our business practices, products and services to provide
you with the very best.

Delivering world-class large format scanners to over 100 countries, Contex solutions are recognized
by a wide range of industries for reliability, high performance and superb image quality.

software for more than 100 years.

your printer is compatible with our scanners is a big part of that quest. That is why we collaborate

### Electrode localization

You have only one opportunity -- make the most of it! You took the time to position the electrodes
accurately, so it should be worth the time to measure their locations with respect to surface
landmarks to enhance future signal analysis options.  3D locations of electrodes can be used in
co-registration of surface measured physiological signals with anatomical MRI, CT and other imaging
modalities in software applications such as EMSE Suite and others.  Quick and accurate measurement
of 3D electrode positions adds only 3-5 minutes to a typical study, but it ensures precision when
coregistering surface measurements with anatomical images.

# Research

Sleep fulfills vital functions for the brain and body. However, sleep is not a uniform state:
alternating substates and oscillation patterns show rich variations on different time scales. In the
Sleep & Memory Lab, based at the [Donders Institute][8] in Nijmegen, The Netherlands, we aim to
uncover the mechanisms behind this variability and their specific role in the functions of sleep. We
are particularly interested in the following topics:

─────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[[sle│[**Sleep physiology.**][10] From an evolutionary point of view, spending hours in a           
ep]][│non-responsive state seems strikingly non-adaptive. Sleep thus serves several vital functions 
9]   │to overcompensate for this disadvantage. In our lab, we develop new strategies to understand  
     │the structure of sleep on the micro- (sleep stages and microprocesses), meso- (sleep cycles), 
     │and macro-level (sleep regularity), with the aim to map the richness of sleep physiology to   
     │the different functions of sleep.                                                             
─────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[[cli│[**Clinical applications.**][12] Sleep disturbances are the leading transdiagnostic symptom of
nical│and likely causal contributor to the development of psychiatric and neurological diseases. We 
]][11│focus in particular on two areas of mental health to help translate sleep research insights   
]    │into clinical applications and health care innovations: How is sleep involved stress-related  
     │disorders, and how is brain clearance during sleep impaired in neurodegenerative diseases?    
─────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[[met│[**Sleep research methods.**][14] Polysomnography as the gold standard in sleep research      
hods]│generates rich and multimodal datasets. However, considering the massive costs and thus       
][13]│resulting small sample sizes of this method, we help to transfer sleep research from          
     │small-scale lab environments to large-scale clinical and home settings. We develop and        
     │validate new tools for the recording and analysis of sleep data, from minimal sleep EEG       
     │headbands to analysis pipelines for big sleep data.                                           
─────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[[luc│[**Dreaming.**][16] Conscious experience fluctuates considerably across the sleep-wake cycle: 
id   │alert attention alternates with mind wandering, sleep onset imagery, dreamless sleep and vivid
dream│dreaming. We study consciousness during sleep, considering the phenomenon of lucid dreaming   
ing]]│particularly interesting as both a model case and tool. In addition to fundamental insights   
[15] │into the functions and neural correlates of dreaming, we develop and validate different dream 
     │engineering strategies to modulate dream experiences.                                         
─────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[[mne│[**Memory.**][18] Memory skills differ across the general population – from age-related memory
monic│decline to the outstanding feats of memory champions. In addition to the role of sleep in     
s]][1│memory processing, we investigate different strategies of learning and memory enhancement,    
7]   │with a focus on the mnemonic training strategies used in memory sports. Beyond the efficacy of
     │mnemonics in naïve subjects, developmental contexts and age-related decline, we are           
     │particularly interested in the neural mechanisms underlying mnemonic training and superior    
     │memory skills.                                                                                
─────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Precision In Neuroscience

## Advancing medicine through the provision of precision imaging biomarker insights for the
## discovery, development and delivery of novel treatments in neurological disease

[ IXI™ Platform ][59]
[ Services ][60]

## A global leader in neuroimaging and biomarker analytics

[ Company ][61]

IXI™ is IXICO’s proprietary, AI-enabled neuroimaging technology platform for precision medicine,
purpose-built to drive clinical trial imaging and biomarker science insights in neurological disease
research.

The Platform, combined with IXICO's expert clinical trial operations, helps accelerate
decision-making in clinical research and maximise the potential of drug development programmes.

## Neuroscience Expertise

IXICO has built a global reputation as a leading end-to-end Imaging Contract Research Organisation
(iCRO), expertly managing and analysing neurological clinical trials.

The Company is a key part of the global neurological disease research community, with a 20-year
proven track record in the biopharmaceutical industry, working with leading pharma companies,
innovative biotechs, scientific consortia, and non-profit organisations.

[ Therapeutic Expertise ][62]

## Differentiated Technology

[ IXI™ Platform ][63]

The IXI™ Platform is tailor-made for neurological diseases, reliably managing global clinical trial
data, precisely reading radiological scans, and measuring key imaging biomarkers linked to the
identification, progression, and treatment of conditions such as Alzheimer’s, Huntington’s, and
Parkinson’s disease.

# Precision In Neuroscience

## Advancing medicine through the provision of precision imaging biomarker insights for the
## discovery, development and delivery of novel treatments in neurological disease

[ IXI™ Platform ][59]
[ Services ][60]

## A global leader in neuroimaging and biomarker analytics

[ Company ][61]

IXI™ is IXICO’s proprietary, AI-enabled neuroimaging technology platform for precision medicine,
purpose-built to drive clinical trial imaging and biomarker science insights in neurological disease
research.

The Platform, combined with IXICO's expert clinical trial operations, helps accelerate
decision-making in clinical research and maximise the potential of drug development programmes.

## Neuroscience Expertise

IXICO has built a global reputation as a leading end-to-end Imaging Contract Research Organisation
(iCRO), expertly managing and analysing neurological clinical trials.

The Company is a key part of the global neurological disease research community, with a 20-year
proven track record in the biopharmaceutical industry, working with leading pharma companies,
innovative biotechs, scientific consortia, and non-profit organisations.

[ Therapeutic Expertise ][62]

## Differentiated Technology

[ IXI™ Platform ][63]

The IXI™ Platform is tailor-made for neurological diseases, reliably managing global clinical trial
data, precisely reading radiological scans, and measuring key imaging biomarkers linked to the
identification, progression, and treatment of conditions such as Alzheimer’s, Huntington’s, and
Parkinson’s disease.

# Defining the future of brain health

The only technology for accessible and evidence-based measurements of the brain.

[Experience it yourself][7]

## The core principles behind our products

### Actionable

Leveraging advanced algorithms to drive improvements in brain health and develop new interventions.

[Offer Kernel Scans at your clinic →][8]

### Science-backed

We lead with robust science and engage with leaders in the community.

[Read our publications →][9]

### Differentiated

A deep technology platform that both scales and breaks through the limitations of those that came
before.

[Learn more about the technology →][10]

## From brain data to insight

Kernel delivers detailed information about brain function by combining our non-invasive brain
measurements with algorithmic advances. You can now reliably track the performance of your brain.
1. Book a scan with one of our partner clinics
2. Get scanned in 30 minutes or less
3. Review your results with our user-friendly reports
4. Consult with your health team and see how interventions change your brain health

[Find a location][11][See what to expect][12]
[Platform]

## Follow your brain function over time

Unlike genetics, our brains are constantly changing and regular measurement is important to
understand what factors create the biggest changes in function.

Kernel's longitudinal reports let you visualize your cognitive health so you and your clinician can
track these changes, measure progress, and optimize interventions.

## Built for wellness and medicine

Discover our industry-leading tracer wellness products and learn more about our
upcoming marer medical products.

[Wellness]
[Wellness]

### Brain Agetracer

We track our step count and sleep quality, now you can track your brain health. Brain Age is an
objective measure of health built from thousands of scans.

[Book a scan with one of our clinics →][13]

### Cognitiontracer

The only cognitive tracker designed to assess healthy brains. Receive a detailed composition report
of key cognitive domains and see how your cognitive performance stacks up to others.

[Book a scan with one of our clinics →][14]

### Depressionmarer

Our depression study investigates whether brain activity can help predict if patients will respond
to TMS and Spravato® (esketamine) treatments. Early results suggest Kernel Flow may offer new
insights for selecting the right treatment for the right patient at the right time.

[Learn more about our ongoing work →][15]

### Cognitionmarer

In a published study, Kernel Flow successfully detected early patterns of brain activity associated
with mild cognitive impairment (MCI). This result highlights the platform's potential to support
early identification of cognitive decline in clinical settings. Additional studies are being planned
to assess more detailed profiles of cognitive performance in the context of disease diagnostics.

[Read our recent publication →][16]

### Research Opportunities

Want to participate in a paid research study that helps our team develop the next generation of
brain health tools?

[Visit KerneLabs to learn more →][17]

#### [ From Compliance to Clinical Action: Fixing the Broken Loop in Post-Market Surveillance ][24]

By Aalap Patel, MS, CQE, CSSBB

Post-market surveillance (PMS) systems in the medical device industry have become increasingly
sophisticated in collecting complaints, monitoring adverse events, and generating regulatory
reports. However, many organizations still struggle to translate these insights into timely clinical
action and meaningful patient safety improvements. This article examines the growing disconnect
between regulatory reporting and operational decision-making, explores the challenges of signal
detection and prioritization, and outlines practical strategies for building closed-loop PMS systems
that improve patient safety outcomes and organizational responsiveness.

### Why Neuroimaging

Neuroimaging can play a role in drug development at all stages of the process, pre-clinical to phase
IV.  In pre-clinical it can be used for validating animal models.  In phase I, it can be used to
better establish dose response curves, aid in the shifting the proof of concept (POC) from late to
early phase, and identifying additional/alternative targets for late stage study.  In phases II &
III, it can aid and/or serve, thanks to the recent passage of passage of the 21st Century Cures
Act[^{I}][1], as proof of efficacy.  In phase IV, it can be used to provide differentiation between
available treatments.

Focusing here just on POC, the CNS drug pipeline has stymied, with CNS drugs 45% less likely to
proceed to regulatory filling than non-CNS drugs[^{II}][2]. Failures in CNS drugs are due in large
part to failures to demonstrate efficacy in Phase III, with rates significantly higher than non-CNS
drugs[^{II}][3]. While phase III attrition rates are significantly higher for CNS drugs, it is not
the case for phase II. Putting it in other words CNS drugs fail late in trials predominately for
efficacy when compared to other drugs. These late stage failures are costly both in time and in
dollars.

#### Dwindling Numbers Along the CNS Drug Pipeline[^{iii}][4]^{,}[^{v}][5]

Figure 1: Dwindling Numbers in the traditional CNS Drug Discovery Pipeline. For CNS drugs the
average discontinuation rate for the clinical trial phase is 99.6%.

#### Reasons for Phase III Discontinuations[^{II}][6]

Figure 2: Proportion of Phase III discontinuations by primary cause.

To quote the former director of National Institutes of Mental Health (NIMH), Dr. Thomas
Insel[^{III}][7], “Given that over 95% of compounds fail during the clinical phases of development
(a fact not appreciated by looking at the published literature which is biased towards positive
results), success may require rapid failures in order to conserve resources by moving quickly to the
next candidate (“fast-fail”[^{IV}][8])."  The “fast-fail, quick win” model (see figure below) is one
where the proof of concept (POC) is shifted earlier in the clinical trials, from phases II & III to
phase I, from on or after the first effective dose (FED) to the first human dose (FHD) or shortly
thereafter.

Shifting the POC earlier, will increase attrition in earlier stages, but will also increase the
probability of success in the new molecular entities (NME’s) that make it through phase I.  This
“fast-fail” approach allows a culling of the pipeline early on, reducing cost[^{V}][9].  The savings
estimate due to this shift is on the order of $30 Million dollars in out-of-pocket expenses per
NME[^{IV}][10].  This savings can be used to fund approximately 2 additional NME phase I
studies[^{IV}][11].

#### Quick Win - Fast Fail Model^{[III][12]}

Figure 3: Paul, S., et al.'s Quick Win / Fast-Fail Model - The idea behind it is to shift the Proof
of Concept (POC) in human for new molecular entities from phases II & III in clinical trials to
phase I. By shifting the POC earlier the attrition in can be shifted earlier leading to a higher
probability of success in later stages, in turn leading to tremendous savings in time and money. In
addition, to shifting attrition, NMEs can readily returned to preclinical stages if alternative
targets are found during phase I.

This POC shift to early phase requires the support of surrogate measures. Positron Emission
Tomography (PET) has long been considered the main avenue for surrogate makers in CNS clinical
trials, whether through biodistribution, receptor occupancy/binding or measuring metabolic changes
in the target using FDG or FDOPA[^{VI}][13].  Unfortunately, biodistribution and receptor
occupancy/binding are only a part of a POC, that is, they show that the drug in question is finding
the target, but show nothing on whether or not it is modulating the target circuit in a meaningful
way.  FDG & FDOPA have the potential to measure target modulation, but they are slow (low temporal
resolution) and blunt (low spatial resolution) tools, and as such they miss many meaningful
signals.  Where PET fails in measuring functional change other neuroimaging modalities can be
brought to bear.  These include but are not limited to: fMRI, ASL, qEEG, EEG-fMRI, EEG source
imaging, NIRS, & MEG.

#### What is Functional Neuroimaging & What can it do

FMRI and other imaging modalities such as qEEG, EEG-fMRI, EEG source, MEG and NIRS are quantitative
based tools, providing researchers and business leaders with statistical decision making power.

Insel[^{III}][7], “Given that over 95% of compounds fail during the clinical phases of development
(a fact not appreciated by looking at the published literature which is biased towards positive
results), success may require rapid failures in order to conserve resources by moving quickly to the
next candidate (“fast-fail”[^{IV}][8])."  The “fast-fail, quick win” model (see figure below) is one
where the proof of concept (POC) is shifted earlier in the clinical trials, from phases II & III to
phase I, from on or after the first effective dose (FED) to the first human dose (FHD) or shortly
thereafter.

Shifting the POC earlier, will increase attrition in earlier stages, but will also increase the
probability of success in the new molecular entities (NME’s) that make it through phase I.  This
“fast-fail” approach allows a culling of the pipeline early on, reducing cost[^{V}][9].  The savings
estimate due to this shift is on the order of $30 Million dollars in out-of-pocket expenses per
NME[^{IV}][10].  This savings can be used to fund approximately 2 additional NME phase I
studies[^{IV}][11].

#### Quick Win - Fast Fail Model^{[III][12]}

Figure 3: Paul, S., et al.'s Quick Win / Fast-Fail Model - The idea behind it is to shift the Proof
of Concept (POC) in human for new molecular entities from phases II & III in clinical trials to
phase I. By shifting the POC earlier the attrition in can be shifted earlier leading to a higher
probability of success in later stages, in turn leading to tremendous savings in time and money. In
addition, to shifting attrition, NMEs can readily returned to preclinical stages if alternative
targets are found during phase I.

This POC shift to early phase requires the support of surrogate measures. Positron Emission
Tomography (PET) has long been considered the main avenue for surrogate makers in CNS clinical
trials, whether through biodistribution, receptor occupancy/binding or measuring metabolic changes
in the target using FDG or FDOPA[^{VI}][13].  Unfortunately, biodistribution and receptor
occupancy/binding are only a part of a POC, that is, they show that the drug in question is finding
the target, but show nothing on whether or not it is modulating the target circuit in a meaningful
way.  FDG & FDOPA have the potential to measure target modulation, but they are slow (low temporal
resolution) and blunt (low spatial resolution) tools, and as such they miss many meaningful
signals.  Where PET fails in measuring functional change other neuroimaging modalities can be
brought to bear.  These include but are not limited to: fMRI, ASL, qEEG, EEG-fMRI, EEG source
imaging, NIRS, & MEG.

#### What is Functional Neuroimaging & What can it do

FMRI and other imaging modalities such as qEEG, EEG-fMRI, EEG source, MEG and NIRS are quantitative
based tools, providing researchers and business leaders with statistical decision making power.

Since its inception roughly 25 years ago functional magnetic resonance imagining (fMRI)
[^{VII}][14]^{, } [^{VIII}][15]^{, &} [^{IX}][16] has opened up a new realm of possibilities with
neuroimaging. It has confirmed[^{X}][17], debunked[^{XI}][18] as well as opened new
understandings[^{XII}][19] of how the mind works. When taking the whole family of non-invasive
neuroimaging modalities into account it has by far the highest spatial resolution with some studies
using resolutions on the order of sub millimeter[^{X}][20]. With all of its accolades and the
beautiful pictures it creates, fMRI still has highly limited temporal resolution with the current
upper limit of its sampling rate being on the order of hundreds of milliseconds[^{XIII}][21].

Electroencephalography (EEG) fMRI’s much older cousin has been around for over a century[^{XIV}][22]
and gave some of the first views into the active mind. Even now it is still the key measurement for
sleep staging[^{XV}][23]^{, }[^{XVI}][24] and for diagnosing many neurological disorders such as
epilepsy[^{XVII}][25] and schizophrenia[^{XVIII}][26]. EEG, whose instrumentation is technologically
primitive when compared with that of fMRI, leaves it in the proverbial dust in that EEG has
essentially limitless temporal resolution. EEG spatial resolution on the other hand is more of an
inference than a certainty in that in its native domain it a measurement of electrical potential
differences on the scalp. Transforming these measures across the scalp into the space of the brain
is done through a process referred to as source localization. Source localization’s resolution is on
the order of one to two centimeters[^{XIX}][27].

[Graphic for MRIcroGL]

# MRIcroGL

MRIcroGL allows you to view 2D slices and renderings of your brain imaging data. It can display many
image formats and includes a graphical interface for dcm2nii to convert DICOM images to NIfTI
format. It allows you to draw regions of interest which can aid lesion mapping and fMRI analysis. It
provides sophisticated rendering.

Featured tool/resource

[Graphic for eeg_pipelines]

# eeg_pipelines

This repository contains 4 stand-alone pipelines (along with one test dataset), in EEGLAB,
Fieldtrip, Brainstorm, and MNE. There is also a link to the HAPPE EEGLAB-based pipeline. The
pipelines have been optimized to process event-related potential and are described in the associated
manuscript. All pipelines run on the sample data provided although they do require a separate
installation of the corresponding software packages.

Based on our scanning of the hyperparameter space for artifact rejection and preprocessing, these
are the best automated EEG pipelines for EEGLAB, Fieldtrip, Brainstorm, and MNE to process ERP. Test
them yourself by plugging in your data.

Featured tool/resource

[Graphic for BabelBrain: Planning software for Transcranial Ultrasound Stimulation]

# BabelBrain: Planning software for Transcranial Ultrasound Stimulation

BabelBrain is an open-source standalone graphic-user-interface application designed for studies of
neuromodulation using transcranial ultrasound stimulation (TUS). It calculates the transmitted
acoustic field in the brain tissue, taking into account the distortion effects caused by the skull
barrier. The simulation is prepared using scans from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and, if
available, computed tomography (CT) and zero-echo time MRI scans. It also calculates the thermal
effects based on a given ultrasound regime, such as the total duration of exposure, the duty cycle,
and acoustic intensity. The tool is designed to work in tandem with neuronavigation and
visualization software, such as 3DSlicer. BabelBrain supports multiple GPU backends, including
Metal, OpenCL, and CUDA, and works on all major operating systems, including Linux, macOS, and
Windows. This tool is particularly optimized for Apple ARM64 systems, which are common in brain
imaging research.

Featured tool/resource

[Graphic for BrainEffeX]

# BrainEffeX

Effect size estimation is crucial for power analysis and experiment deisgn, but poses unique
challenges in fMRI research due to the complexity of the data and analysis techniques. Here, we
utalized large fMRI datasets to obtain precise univariate and multivariate effect size estimates
from "typical" fMRI study designs: brain-behavior correlation, task vs. rest, and between-group
analyses of functional connecitivity and task-based activation maps. This is an interactive web
application for exploring these effect maps.

[Graphic for MRIcroGL]

# MRIcroGL

MRIcroGL allows you to view 2D slices and renderings of your brain imaging data. It can display many
image formats and includes a graphical interface for dcm2nii to convert DICOM images to NIfTI
format. It allows you to draw regions of interest which can aid lesion mapping and fMRI analysis. It
provides sophisticated rendering.

Featured tool/resource

[Graphic for eeg_pipelines]

# eeg_pipelines

This repository contains 4 stand-alone pipelines (along with one test dataset), in EEGLAB,
Fieldtrip, Brainstorm, and MNE. There is also a link to the HAPPE EEGLAB-based pipeline. The
pipelines have been optimized to process event-related potential and are described in the associated
manuscript. All pipelines run on the sample data provided although they do require a separate
installation of the corresponding software packages.

Based on our scanning of the hyperparameter space for artifact rejection and preprocessing, these
are the best automated EEG pipelines for EEGLAB, Fieldtrip, Brainstorm, and MNE to process ERP. Test
them yourself by plugging in your data.

Featured tool/resource

[Graphic for BabelBrain: Planning software for Transcranial Ultrasound Stimulation]

# BabelBrain: Planning software for Transcranial Ultrasound Stimulation

BabelBrain is an open-source standalone graphic-user-interface application designed for studies of
neuromodulation using transcranial ultrasound stimulation (TUS). It calculates the transmitted
acoustic field in the brain tissue, taking into account the distortion effects caused by the skull
barrier. The simulation is prepared using scans from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and, if
available, computed tomography (CT) and zero-echo time MRI scans. It also calculates the thermal
effects based on a given ultrasound regime, such as the total duration of exposure, the duty cycle,
and acoustic intensity. The tool is designed to work in tandem with neuronavigation and
visualization software, such as 3DSlicer. BabelBrain supports multiple GPU backends, including
Metal, OpenCL, and CUDA, and works on all major operating systems, including Linux, macOS, and
Windows. This tool is particularly optimized for Apple ARM64 systems, which are common in brain
imaging research.

Featured tool/resource

[Graphic for BrainEffeX]

# BrainEffeX

Effect size estimation is crucial for power analysis and experiment deisgn, but poses unique
challenges in fMRI research due to the complexity of the data and analysis techniques. Here, we
utalized large fMRI datasets to obtain precise univariate and multivariate effect size estimates
from "typical" fMRI study designs: brain-behavior correlation, task vs. rest, and between-group
analyses of functional connecitivity and task-based activation maps. This is an interactive web
application for exploring these effect maps.

# ABOUT RHOVICA

SoNav Platform : transforming blind neurosurgery into guided precision

#### Today : no visibility

Clinicians treating brain emergencies, such as severe trauma or brain bleeding, need to act quickly
and precisely. Without direct imaging, they rely on pre-acquired CT scans to guide procedures,
images that become unreliable intraoperatively, as brain shift may alter the anatomy any time.

#### Our technology

Rhovica’s instrument-embedded technology is able to continuously capture live data from inside the
brain, delivering real-time imaging of the brain without any external imaging equipment.

####  Patented IP

Rhovica’s core technology is protected by several patent families. The intellectual property is
fully owned by Rhovica Neuoimaging AG, providing a strong foundation for defensible market
positioning.

#### SoNav® I

External Ventricular Drain (EVD) placement is on of the most basic and often performed neurosurgical
procedures and can be life-saving. Freehand bedside EVD placement relies solely anatomical landmarks
with up to 28% misplacement rate, multiple passes and risk of hemorrhage.  

SoNav™  is an innovative EVD catheter equipped with integrated miniaturized sensors providing
real-time visualization of brain ventricule directly at the patient’s bedside. 

Our novel EVD catheter SoNav™ allows a fast and secure placement of external ventricular drains as
well as real-time monitoring after insertion for elevated ICP emergencies. 

# TEAM

Executive Team Advisory Team Board of Directors

#### Dr. med. Martin Hlavica

##### Neurosurgeon, Co-Founder & Chief Executive Officer (CEO)

Board-certified neurosurgeon with 500+ neurosurgical interventions, completing residency in
University Hospitals Zurich and Inselspital Bern, driven by evidence-based medicine, (co-)author of
>20 publications in peer-reviewed journals and speaker at international congresses. Ambitious to
make an impact in patient’s treatment with high interest in business creation and economics.
* [ ][15]

#### Blair Fraser, BSc

##### Chief Business Officer (CBO)

Blair has over 35 years of global medical device experience and serves as Chief Business Officer. He
is skilled in a wide range of corporate functions, including general management, global
evidence-based marketing, strategic analysis and planning, mergers, acquisitions and strategic
alliances, and scientific and medical affairs. He has experience of start-up, rapid growth, and
established MedTech companies, with a proven track record of new market identification, penetration
with new technologies, KOL network building, and sustainably increasing market share.
* [ ][16]

#### Dr. med. univ. Thomas Rhomberg

##### Neurosurgeon, Co-Founder & Chief Medical Officer (CMO)

Thomas Rhomberg is the company`s co-founder and board-certified Neurosurgeon currently working as an
attending Neurosurgeon in Austria. He completed his MD from the Medical University of Innsbruck with
a research exchange at the Harvard Medical School. Previous parts of his neurosurgical were
completed at the University Hospital of Bern (Inselspital) and the Kantonsspital St. Gallen. He is
driven by the desire to translate the latest technology into improved patient care.
* [ ][17]

#### Saeid Kasiri, PhD

##### Chief Technology Officer (CTO)

Engineer by training, Saeid has over 15 years of R&D experience in leading and developing Class
II/III medical devices, including active, implantable, and catheter-based technologies. He has
dedicated most of his career to startups and SMEs, with a successful track record of leading
cross-functional teams, design control, and risk management. Saeid translates unmet clinical needs
into innovative and effective design solutions.
* [ ][18]

#### Martin Fuchs

##### Vice President Quality, Governance & Compliance

Martin Fuchs has many years of sales experience in the healthcare sector and is experienced in
conception and realization of eHealth software solutions and Quality Systems.

### [EHA 2026 | BRUIN CLL-322: Clinical Outcome Analysis Report][23]

Abstract: EHA-7224 Short: LB5001 BRUIN CLL-322 (NCT04965493) is the first randomized Phase 3 trial
to evaluate a non-covalent BTK inhibitor–based triplet regimen in previously treated CLL/SLL. With a
data cutoff of February 2, 2026, and results presented at EHA 2026, the trial demonstrated that
fixed-duration pirtobrutinib + venetoclax–rituximab (PVR) significantly improved progression-free
survival over venetoclax–rituximab (VenR) alone, meeting its primary endpoint across all key
subgroups. Overall survival data were not yet mature but trended in favor of PVR. This represents
Lilly's fourth Phase 3 CLL win for pirtobrutinib (Jaypirca®) and positions PVR as a potential new
standard of care in the relapsed/refractory setting.

You are only a few clicks away from our highly experienced diagnostic imaging and neurology experts

highly experienced neurology and neuroimaging experts can provide you with a detailed imaging
report, as well as practical advice on the best way forward to manage your patients, and if needed,
most adequate neurosurgical technique.
